artifacts.summary: Design: detect a fresh (untracked) specs tree via git ls-files; write a repo-root .gitignore managed block with a single /specs/ line only in that case, since only a repo-root-level rule can make specs_tree_is_gitignored() (task 658's predicate) report the tree ignored; an already-tracked consumer's specs/.gitignore-only behavior is preserved unchanged; flags check-runtime-file-tracking.sh Check C as a follow-on gap outside file_scope.

memory_candidates.content: git check-ignore -q -- specs (run from repo root) only ever returns 0 if a .gitignore AT OR ABOVE the repo root matches the bare 'specs' path -- a pattern confined to specs/.gitignore itself cannot produce this result, since check-ignore resolves the ancestor-directory chain from the tested path's parent upward, not from inside the directory being tested. Verified live in a scratch repo: root .gitignore containing '/specs/' makes check-ignore -q -- specs exit 0; this repo's own tracked-specs root (no such root-level rule) exits 1. This is the mechanism scripts/lib/specs-ignore-lib.sh's specs_tree_is_gitignored() depends on, and any future 'ignore this whole subtree' design must place the rule at or above the subtree's own level, never inside it.

scripts/lib/deploy-baseline-lib.sh's DEPLOY_BASELINE_GOVERNING_SOURCES table attributes any *.gitignore/*.lock/*/000_probe/* lint finding to a fixed 4-file group (runtime-file-patterns.sh, init-specs.sh, orchestrator-runtime-files.md, check-runtime-file-tracking.sh) even though a given task's own file_scope may name only 3 of the 4. This is useful signal that a change confined to a narrower file_scope is still correctly attributed by the baseline system, but it does NOT mean the 4th file's own invariants (e.g. check-runtime-file-tracking.sh's Check C) get updated automatically -- that still requires an explicit edit or a recorded, deliberate gap.
